Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking the time on the call earlier. As discussed, procurement needs a baseline rate card for the hosted API (token pricing, embedding units, and overage rules) and our legal team will need an NDA before we can share internal traffic volumes.

Can you send your standard commercial rate card and your NDA template? Our expected starting volumes are ~750k tokens/month with an option to expand to 2M in Q3. Also: do you have an expiration on the rate quote, and can you note any committed usage discounts?

If useful, looping in Samir from procurement (cc'ed). Looking to get this over the finish line in the next two weeks.

Thanks,

Hi Laura —

Thanks, attached is the signed NDA via DocuSign (Skyline_signed_NDA_v1.pdf). We signed without redlines so you should be able to proceed with the ratecard.

A couple of specific questions we'll need addressed in the ratecard:
- Do token counts include embeddings calls or are those billed separately?
- Is there a separate unit for streaming responses?
- Do you offer a committed-capacity SKU (reserved GPU/dedicated pool) vs hosted on-demand, and are those priced differently on this ratecard?

Also, what flexibility do you have on a first-year discount for committed volume — we are leaning toward a 12-month commit but want to understand the commercial levers.

If possible, can you send the ratecard and a short summary of the tiered discount table?

Appreciate it — Maria

Karthik / Aditya —

Skyline returned the signed NDA (attached to the thread). They asked for the hosted API baseline ratecard and specifically called out committed capacity vs on-demand pricing, embeddings, and streaming units. Their expected starting volume is ~750k tokens/month with a potential bump to ~2M by Q3.

Can you review and confirm the following for me before I send the customer the ratecard PDF (I plan to send v3):
- Can we offer a 15% first-year discount on a 12-month 1M token/month commitment?
- If not, would 12% + 99.9% SLA be acceptable?
- Confirm whether embeddings are billed as separate embedding-units (per 1k vectors) or included in token counts for Skyline's use-case.

I attached the draft ratecard (Skyline_Redwood_Ratecard_v3.pdf) and a short note with pricing rationale (rate_notes_karthik.txt). I need to reply to Maria with the official PDF and a summary table by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks — Laura

Attachments: Skyline_Redwood_Ratecard_v3.pdf, rate_notes_karthik.txt
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-22T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Skyline NDA received — need ratecard v3 and discount guidance

Laura —

Reviewed the draft. Notes below (copy for the thread / audit trail):
- 15% on 1M tokens/month looks aggressive for a first-year new enterprise; recommend 12% for 12-month commit, 15% only on 24-month or larger.
- Add an expiry date to the ratecard (45–60 days). I suggest 60 days since procurement timelines can be slow.
- Clarify embeddings: bill as separate embedding-units (per 1k vectors) — include a worked example for a typical dev flow.
- Call out streaming token multipliers in the appendix (some customers see 1.2–1.5x token-equivalent for streaming sessions).
- Add an explicit note about test credits (one-time 30-day $5k credit) and a pilot pricing path.

I attached my short notes (rate_notes_karthik.txt). If you want to push to 15% on 12 months for strategic reasons, we need approval from RevOps — I'd rather present 12% + 99.9% SLA and let them ask for a trade (e.g. extended commit term or case studies).

Karthik
Head of Pricing & Commercial Ops

Subject: Hosted API ratecard (v3) & discount options — Skyline Health

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for sending the countersigned NDA. Per the internal review, attaching the official Skyline-tailored ratecard (Skyline_Redwood_Ratecard_v3.pdf). Key takeaways (short):

- Ratecard version: v3 (doc id: RC-V3-20270222)
- Expiry: 60 days from today (expires 2027-04-23)
- Baseline hosted API pricing: token generation $0.0008 / token; embeddings priced at $0.0035 per 1k vectors (separate unit). Streaming sessions have a multiplier noted in appendix.
- Discount options for committed usage (applies to token-generation portion only):
  * 12-month 1M token/month commit: 12% discount
  * 24-month 1M token/month commit: 15% discount
  * 3-month pilot: 6% discount (pilot credits available)
- Pilot credit: one-time $5k evaluation credit applied to first invoice for new customers
- Committed capacity (Reserved / Dedicated) pricing is available as a separate SKU — we'll provide a follow-up proposal if Skyline prefers reserved pools.

Next steps:
1) If the pricing above looks good, we can send a DocuSign commitment (I can draft the commercial SOW and term sheet). HubSpot deal id: HS-293847.
2) If you want a counter-proposal, please send suggested redlines; for any pricing increases we’ll need RevOps sign-off.
3) Happy to schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through the rate table and worked examples.

I included Karthik and Aditya on the thread for transparency.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Rep, Redwood Inference
